findings.issue: The Grant object's `id` is populated with the NIH RePORTER project-details URL (https://reporter.nih.gov/project-details/10472824). This is a landing page for the project record, not an identifier for the grant as an entity; the bundle supplies explicit grant identifiers (project number 1OT2OD032701-01, core project number OT2OD032701, application ID 10472824) which are relegated to free-text `notes`. Under the v3 rule, declared fields should carry the structured content rather than prose. Same defect present in the core record.
Identical to the full record: grant identity carried by a resolver URL while the attested award numbers sit in prose `notes`.

`CTP-deid` is entered as a machine annotation tool with the description 'CHoRUS repository supporting de-identification of clinical imaging data.' The bundle lists CTP-deid in the chorus-ai repository listing with no description whatsoever. The record's own `source_caveats` concedes the role is inferred from the repository name. This is an unsupported inference about what a tool does; the evidence boundary favors omission. Same defect in the core record.
Identical unsupported inference about CTP-deid's function, self-declared as inferred in its own source_caveats.

`counts: 7642` is attached to an instance declared as 'Radiology imaging study extracted from hospital PACS'. The bundle states '7,642 Admissions with Radiology Data' — a count of admissions, not of imaging studies. The instance_type and the count denominate different units. The trailing `notes` acknowledges the mismatch rather than resolving it; the instance_type should name the admission-with-imaging unit if the count is retained. Same defect in the core record.
Same unit mismatch: count of admissions with radiology data attached to an instance typed as an imaging study.

The six named individuals are the 'Bridge2AI CHoRUS Leadership Team' as listed in the cohort 2 webinar. The bundle nowhere describes them as members of a data access or governance committee; the record's own source_caveats states no formally named data access committee is described. Populating `committee_members` with a leadership roster asserts a governance structure the bundle does not attest. Same defect in the core record.
Same: leadership-team roster placed in `committee_members` while the record's caveat concedes no access committee is described in the bundle.

Ciera McCrary is identified in the bundle as 'MGH, Program Manager' under a 'Contact Us' heading on the project website. She is not attested as a contact for any governance or access committee; the bundle's stated access-request contacts are dbold@emory.edu and jared.houghtaling@tuftsmedicine.org. Assigning her to `committee_contact` overstates the role the bundle supports. Same defect in the core record.
Same role overstatement for the program-manager contact placed in `committee_contact`.

`is_direct: false` is a boolean assertion the bundle does not make; the record's own source_caveats states the value is inferred and that 'the sources do not use the terms direct or third-party collection.' A self-declared inference in a boolean slot is an unsupported claim rather than a caveated one. Note this slot is present in the full record only.

`was_reported_by_subjects: false` is asserted with no supporting statement in the bundle. The sources describe retrospective extraction from hospital systems but never address whether any element (e.g. nursing flowsheet entries capturing patient-reported symptoms, demographics) originated as subject report. Prefer omission. Same defect in the core record.
Same unsupported negative boolean assertion.

`at_risk_groups_included: true` is derived from the presence of PICU and NICU admissions. The bundle states PICU/NICU coverage but never characterizes any population as at-risk, nor does it use that framing. The `special_protections` entry likewise repackages general controlled-access statements as protections for at-risk groups, which the bundle does not connect to minors. Same defect in the core record.
Same: at-risk framing and group-specific protections constructed from general access-control statements the bundle does not tie to minors.

The EthicalReview object carries no ethics review at all — its own source_caveats states 'no institutional review board approval or ethics committee determination is reported in the bundle.' The `review_details` value describes the project's ethics research pillar (focus groups, legal-landscape analysis), which is not an ethical review of the dataset. Under the v2 rule, a value recording that something exists elsewhere or is absent has not answered the field; the slot should be omitted. Same defect in the core record.
Same: ethics-program description occupying a slot that asks for ethical review, with the record itself conceding no review is reported.

The object populates `involves_human_subjects` and `special_populations` but its source_caveats concedes no IRB approval or ethics board is stated. More materially, the bundle never states that the dataset constitutes human subjects research — it states the data are patient data collected retrospectively. `involves_human_subjects: true` is a regulatory determination the bundle does not make. Same in core.
Same: regulatory determination asserted as a boolean where the bundle supplies only the fact that the data are patient-derived.

`https://chorus4ai.org/#holdout-test-set` is a minted fragment on an attested base URI, which is permitted for a part of this dataset. However the object populates only id/name/description/is_data_split; the bundle supplies no size, composition, or access terms for the holdout set, so the DataSubset carries little beyond a restatement of the description. Borderline rather than defective.

`OTHER` is emitted once to cover both the EDF+/Persyst EEG schemas and the OHNLP note schema — two distinct non-registered standards collapsed into a single enum value. The enum admits no finer distinction, so this is a limitation of the vocabulary rather than a fabrication, but the multivalued slot does not distinguish the two. Same in core.

`status` has range string and its description offers examples of the draft/published/deprecated kind. The value here is a two-clause narrative sentence about ongoing acquisition. The content is bundle-supported but the slot is being used as a progress note rather than a status token; the narrative duplicates material already in `updates.update_details`. Same in core.
Same: narrative progress sentence in a status slot, duplicating updates.update_details.

Each DistributionFormat object populates only `format`, and packs three separate facts into that one string — the format/schema, the access control level, and the metadata-publication state. The class declares `media_type` and the access-control content belongs to governance slots rather than to a format description. Nine objects repeat the same 'controlled access' clause already stated in license_and_use_terms and regulatory_restrictions. Same in core.
Same overloading of the `format` string with access-control and metadata-status content across all nine objects.

Every Creator object uses `principal_investigator` for all six named individuals. The bundle designates only Eric S. Rosenthal as principal investigator (NIH RePORTER); the other five are listed as 'Bridge2AI CHoRUS Leadership Team' members in the webinar slide, with no PI designation. Typing all six as principal_investigator overstates five of them. Same in core.
Same: five leadership-team members typed as principal_investigator without bundle support.

The maintainer_details string embeds the commentary-flagged email 'cmccrary@mgh.havard.edu' inline. The typo is separately flagged in the sibling source_caveats, so the transcription is defensible, but embedding a contact address plus a person's name and role in a free-text details field where the class offers no structured contact field means the identity is carried only as prose. Minor. Same in core.

'at 14 contributing hospitals in the United States' — the bundle attests 14 contributing hospitals and separately gives 'United States of America' as the GitHub organization's location. It does not state that the contributing hospitals are all US-based. The geographic scope claim is an inference, thin though plausible. Same in core.
Same unattested US geographic scoping of the contributing hospitals.

The `notes` slot carries the website banner quotation and the software licensing facts. The MIT/Apache-2.0 licensing of chorus-ai repositories is a fact about software rather than about the dataset; it is correctly kept out of `license`, but `notes` is specified for residual content after every fitting slot is used, and this material is also restated in license_and_use_terms.source_caveats. Duplicative rather than wrong.

The core `notes` adds a sentence not present in the full record's `notes`: 'The project sequesters a holdout test set, drawn from the same collection, for external validation of AI/ML models.' The holdout set is bundle-supported and appears in the full record as `subsets[0]`, so this is not unsupported content, but the core record states it in a slot where the full record does not, and the phrase 'drawn from the same collection' is a compositional claim the bundle does not make explicitly.

The full record carries `subsets` with the holdout test set as a DataSubset; the core record omits the slot and instead mentions the holdout set in prose within `notes`. If CoreDataset declares `subsets`, this is a loss of structure relative to the full record; if it does not, the prose fallback is acceptable. Flagged for reconciliation to confirm against the core schema.

Present in the full record (`is_shared: true` with supporting notes) and absent from the core record. The projection drops a bundle-supported governance fact without an evident reason; confirm whether CoreDataset declares the slot.
Neither record populates these, correctly — the bundle supports none of them. Noted only to confirm the omissions were audited and are not gaps.

summary: Both records are substantially faithful to the declared bundle in their narrative content, and the two are near-identical in wording, so almost every finding applies to both. No fabricated organizational or personal registry identifiers were found, no resolver URL appears in a uriorcurie slot where a declared prefix would fit, no enum value outside the permitted lists is used, and no prose appears where the schema requires a list. The dominant defect class is caveated inference: eight slots (direct_collection.is_direct, acquisition_methods[0].was_reported_by_subjects, at_risk_populations.at_risk_groups_included, human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects, machine_annotation_tools[2] CTP-deid, ethical_reviews[0], data_governance.committee_members, data_governance.committee_contact) assert content the bundle does not state, several of them in boolean fields where a source_caveats note cannot soften the assertion, and several self-declaring the inference in their own caveats. Under the evidence boundary these should be omitted rather than hedged. The second class is structural: grant identity carried by a RePORTER landing-page URL while the attested award numbers (1OT2OD032701-01, OT2OD032701, application 10472824) sit in prose notes; nine DistributionFormat objects overloading the `format` string with access-control and metadata-status content; all six creators typed as principal_investigator when the bundle designates only Rosenthal. One unit mismatch: 7,642 is a count of admissions with radiology data but is attached to an instance typed as an imaging study. Core-versus-full divergence is small — the core notes slot adds a holdout-set sentence the full notes lacks (the fact is in the full record's subsets slot), and the core drops subsets and third_party_sharing; these three should be reconciled against the CoreDataset slot inventory in Phase 4. The tier-2-over-tier-4 disagreement on released admission counts (50,000 versus over 45K) is correctly resolved and documented in source_caveats on both records.
